turns.text: The previous story examined Neural Machine Translation with Attention. Now the camera turns to Highway Networks and a new question along the same timeline: Why did researchers need Highway Networks, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?

The key idea in Highway Networks was to add learnable carry gates to deep networks. When a layer did not need to rewrite information, the model could let signals pass through almost unchanged, turning very deep training from mandatory layer-by-layer rewriting into transformation only when needed.

Its place in deep-learning history is bridge-like: on one side, gating repaired trainability; on the other, ResNet used a simpler shortcut structure to carry the same optimization intuition into the mainstream.
The thread continues with ResNet, where researchers push the problem one step further.
